items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well the only significant engagement was at The Roundtable with Tyree Glen. It was a quartet... I learned a lot with Tyre.

ctx.x: you also worked with J. J. Johnson?
Yes before I worked with J.J. I worked with Tyree Glen ad the round table on 52nd street and Lexington, The Embers was around the corner, all of these clubs. That was educational for me cause-­

items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Henry would come in and sub for Tyree... We got this job... That was 1957 with J.J.

ctx.x: It was 1957. It wasn’t ’59. It was ’57. With Sweets. That was more like ’59. My mind is backwards here. (Laughs) You’re getting me to think about things I haven’t thought about in 30 years.
So after Tyree Glenn, then Henry Sweets Edison seems significant.

Oh yeah, Henry would come in and sub for Tyree and that’s how I got to know him. We got this job—that’s how he knew about me. When he was out on the road he’d always call. If I was available I got the job, if not he got someone else. That was 1957 with J.J. then we toured and went to Sweden from Kiruna to Gothenburg
